----- INCIDENT-DEUTERON DATA
d + d
New evaluation from ENDL2009
P. Navratil, D.A. Brown, C. Hagmann, 26 June 2009
MT=2: elastic scatttering.
All files: Taken from the Evaluated Charged Particle Library
(ECPL) [2].
MT=50: d + d -> n + 3He
Cross-section: Used Descouvemont's [3] S-factor R-matrix fit at
low energies up to 1.96 MeV and use the ECPL evaluation for
energies above 5 MeV. From 1.96 MeV to 5 MeV.  Used spline fit
that matches the two evaluations and also matches a few
experimental points from Ref [4]. Angular distributions are taken
from ECPL [2].
MT=600: d + d -> p + t
Cross-section: Used Descouvemont's [3] S-factor R-matrix fit at
low energies up to 1.96 MeV and use the ECPL evaluation [2] for
energies above 5 MeV. From 1.96 MeV to 5 MeV.  Used spline fit
that matches the two evaluations and also matches a few
experimental points from Ref [4]. Angular distributions are taken
from ECPL [2].
Note: The slight mass differences between the p & n and between
the t & 3He were ignored in the creation of the angular
distributions.  Thus, the proton in the MT=600 file has the same
angular distribution as the neutron in the MT=50 file. Similarly,
the 3He in MT=50 has the same angular distribution as the t in

---- ENDF/B-VIII.1    MATERIAL  131         REVISION 1
----- INCIDENT-DEUTERON DATA
ENDF/B-VIII.1beta3 (G. Hale/M. Paris 2023-Dec):
-MF3 MT51: previously (ENDF/B-VIII.) LR=1; now LR=0, to be more
consistent with [1]; extended for this VIII.1beta3 release to 20
MeV in MF3 (& MF6 -- see below)
-MF3 MT91: T(d,gamma_{0+1}) up to 25 MeV (new for this release)
-MF6 MT51: extended to 20 MeV
-MF6 MT91: included neutron continuum contributions from
LLNL (C. Mattoon/I. Thompson)
[1] C. Poppe et al PR 129, 733, 1963 (Table 1, p.738)
d-t reaction evaluation, based on 5He system R-matrix analysis
by G. Hale (7/94), and T(d,n) Legendre coefficients evaluated by
M. Drosg (6/97).  This version replaces Drosg's 12/94 Legendre
moments for the T(d,n) differential cross section up to 30 MeV by
his new evaluation at energies between 7.5 and 40 MeV.
This evaluation contains integrated cross sections and angular
distributions for the reactions initiated by deuterons on tritons
at deuteron energies up to 10 MeV.  The energy range for the
T(d,n)4He reaction has been extended to 40 MeV by matching to
Legendre coefficients obtained by Drosg.  The information below 10
MeV comes primarily from the solution parameters of an extensive
multi-channel R-matrix analysis of reactions in the 5He system
(including n-alpha elastic scattering) at deuteron energies up to
10 MeV (neutron energies up to 29 MeV), for which chi-square
per degree of freedom is about 1.6.
MF=3, Integrated cross sections:
MT=2, nuclear cross sections for d-t elastic scattering.  The
elastic scattering data set included 675 data points and 5
different types of polarization measurements in addition to the
differential cross sections.
MT=50, T(d,n)4He reaction cross section.  The R-matrix data
set for this reaction contained 1169 data points, including the
recent measurements of the low-energy integrated cross section by
Jarmie and Brown, recent measurements of the differential
cross section in the MeV range by Drosg, and 13 different types
of polarization measurements.  The matching energy for joining
the R-matrix results with Drosg's Legendre coefficients was taken
to be 7 MeV.
MT=51, T(d,n)4He* reaction cross section.  The data set for
this reaction contained 11 data points, including the measurement
of the zero-degree excitation function, and an angular
distribution at one energy, by Poppe.
MF=6,  Legendre coefficients for angular distributions:
MT=2, d+t elastic scattering.  Coefficients are calculated
from the R-matrix fit using the exact (LAW=5) nuclear amplitude
representation (LTP=1).  Nuclear partial waves up through H-
waves were allowed in the analysis, giving Legendre orders
L=0 to 10 in the nuclear cross  section and L=0 to 5 in the
complex nuclear amplitude that interferes with the Coulomb
amplitude.
MT=50, T(d,n)4He reaction.  Coefficients (LAW=2) to L=10 are
given for calculated neutron angular distributions at energies
up to 7 MeV.  Above that energy, the evaluated coefficients of
Drosg `97 are used.  Data included the most recent differential
cross section measurements in the MeV range.  Alpha distributions
are obtained by recoil (LAW=4).
MT=51, T(d,n)4He* reaction.  Two-body (LAW=2) Legendre coef-
ficients are given to L=2 at energies up to 10 MeV.  The decay of
the residual 4He* into p and t is approximated by a phase-space
(LAW=6) representation.
